# Codec export: AV1 and VP9 through bundled SVT-AV1 and libvpx, in MP4 and WebM (road map "codec-export", #377)

- **Status:** Built and closed 2026-10-29, from the owner's brief of 2026-10-27 (#377: "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the encoders."). Each phase was one litecode pipeline with its own review, worked in `~/devel/framejob-codecs` on branch `codecs` (from `75fd806`), and gated, committed and merged into main alone (CX-11). A spike ran before C0 and committed nothing; C5 was rebased onto C6a, so C6a landed first:
  - S, the spike: encoders, containers, alpha, audio, the frame path and HDR measured; no product code
  - C0, CX-1..CX-11 and the encoder build: `make codecs`, SVT-AV1 and libvpx linked into every app (`61a2acc`)
  - C1, AV1 in MP4 at 8 bits, the Speed popup, capped constant quality (CX-12, CX-13) (`3e80381`)
  - C2, AV1 always 10-bit, with HLG, PQ and HDR10 (CX-14) (`5228645`)
  - C3, AV1 in WebM with Opus, through the core's WebM writer (CX-15) (`e759112`)
  - Release items between phases: the acknowledgements (#376), the encoders checked in the published app, the codecs cached in the publish workflow (PUB-10..PUB-12) (`ef3414f`); and #378, one `AVAssetReader` per output in `ExportWriter` (`d0f9fe0`)
  - C4, VP9 in WebM, 8-bit and Profile 2 HDR, and SDR WebM imports labelled (CX-16) (`546df3f`)
  - C6a, the encoder memory limit and the sheet's estimate (CX-18) (`998f0db`)
  - C5, VP9 with alpha in WebM (CX-17) (`cbf6e83`)
  - C6b, 4K on every row and the idle speed figures (CX-18 amended) (`4e01d24`)
  - The close: this record (the commit that moved the original to `archive/`)
- **Original:** `archive/codec-export.md` is the full record. It has no section numbers, so it is cited by its own headings: "orig C3" is its "C3 — AV1 in WebM, with Opus" section, "orig C1 fix pass" that phase's "Fix pass 1", and "orig S §3" the spike's "3. Containers".
- **Spec decisions:** CX-1..CX-18 in spec §11 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`). They stay binding, and where the original or this record words them differently, §11's text wins:
  - CX-1 the four rows (owner); CX-2 SVT-AV1 alone and its three speeds (owner); CX-3 libvpx at one speed (owner); CX-4 the encoders platform-side; CX-5 the build policy; CX-6 the WebM writer in Rust (owner); CX-7 Opus from AudioToolbox; CX-8 HDR; CX-9 the rate model; CX-10 AV1 on M1/M2; CX-11 the working arrangement.
  - CX-12 C1's shape; CX-13 AV1's rate a soft cap, quality first (owner); CX-14 C2's one 10-bit `av1` row; CX-15 C3's `av1_webm`, writer and Opus; CX-16 C4's `vp9_webm` and the SDR import labels; CX-17 C5's `vp9_alpha_webm`; CX-18 C6a's memory limit and estimate, amended by C6b.
  - Amended: CX-5 (by PUB-10); CX-6 and CX-7 (by CX-15); CX-8 (by CX-16); CX-9 (1) and (4) on the AV1 rows (by CX-13); CX-12 (by CX-14, then CX-15); CX-13 (by CX-14); CX-14 (by CX-15); CX-15 (by CX-16, then CX-17); CX-16 (by CX-17); CX-17 (6) (in C5's fix pass, before its code); CX-18 (by C6b). This road map amended HD-5's row list, HD-14 (c), HD-18 (b), HD-19 (b), G-35 and #326's `queued` answer; #378's own §11 entry amends G-17.

## Context

Before this road map Frame Job exported H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. The owner's brief (2026-10-27) asked for AV1 and VP9 with the encoders bundled, and fixed four rows (AV1 in MP4 with AAC, AV1 in WebM with Opus, VP9 in WebM with Opus, VP9 with alpha in WebM; VP9 in MP4 not wanted), SVT-AV1 at three speeds (Faster 8, Balanced 6, Smaller file 4), libvpx at one, and a Rust WebM writer in the core rather than libwebm. The rest were the orchestrator's defaults, each the owner's to change: AudioToolbox's Opus, AV1 HDR first and VP9 Profile 2 later, pinned tarballs with no vendored source, the bitrate semantics kept, the M1/M2 decode gap documented, the encoders platform-side. Standing owner rules applied throughout: only higher-quality exports matter, memory limits relative to physical RAM, no feature size budget, person-only checks in `docs/manual-checks.md`. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices", "The orchestrator's defaults", "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)")

## Decisions

- **SVT-AV1, not libaom (CX-2, the spike).** At matched quality SVT-AV1 preset 4 equalled libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF over HEVC +3.36 against +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 against +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`) at about 41 fps against 13.6–16, about 3× faster; at matched speed SVT 8 gave +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37. libaom's best (good-3/4) is about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. libaom's favour: a higher worst frame (92 against 88) and half the memory. Presets 10 and 12 came within 0.7 VMAF of HEVC: no row. (orig S §2)
- **VP9 is for the web and alpha, not efficiency (CX-3).** libvpx good-4 needs 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality, but 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's; good-2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 % more time, rt-8 only HEVC's quality. (orig S §2)
- **The encoders are static, platform-side, built by `make codecs` (CX-4, CX-5).** No nasm, yasm, meson or ninja is needed on arm64 (Neon C intrinsics); cmake from Homebrew and the system perl are. The cold build is about 30 s; the stamp makes a warm one a no-op. Linked and stripped, SVT-AV1 adds 3.33 MB and libvpx 1.59 MB. `libSvtAv1Enc.a` carries `vector.c` (MIT), whose notice ships only through #376's acknowledgements (PUB-10). (orig S §1, C0)
- **The WebM writer is the core's (CX-6, CX-15).** Container bytes are decisions (timestamps, clusters, cues, CodecDelay), not sample work, as #216-R drew the line; the spike's libwebm files read back through the core's reader, which is the round-trip the core's tests now make against the writer. It is a second `ExportPipeline`, the one exception to §7.8's one writer, sharing the reader outputs, the pump, the gain, #337's end, the chapter partition, the size and the rates. (orig S §3, C3)
- **AV1 in MP4 goes through a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (CX-12).** `canAdd` answered true for `av01`, and every frame decoded md5-identical. The core builds `av1C` from a full parse of the sequence header OBU, strips temporal delimiters and patches the `ftyp` to carry `av01`, which AV1-ISOBMFF requires and `AVAssetWriter` does not write (`rc_av1_*`). The writer reads sync samples from the bitstream itself: both `all-sync` and `no-sync` survived, so the attachment code went and A5's key-flag match is the guard. (orig S §3, C1, C1 fix pass)
- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. Capped CRF replaced it, calibrated so each tier matches or beats HEVC's VMAF at HEVC's rate on the spike's three clips and on the owner's 55 s 1080p clip through the app itself, because SvtAv1EncApp's command-line scores did not transfer (1.1 VMAF lower for SVT-AV1 at one CRF and 1.6 for HEVC on that clip). A strict cap (12 % overshoot) left Faster under HEVC at Format default (a plateau at 95.055–95.348 against 95.469), because SVT-AV1 budgets each window's keyframes and base layers under the cap; SVT's default 50 % overshoot met every comparator. (orig C1 fix pass)
- **`av1` is always 10-bit, an HDR row (CX-14).** AV1's Main profile decodes 8 and 10 bits alike and only higher-quality exports matter, so there is no `av1_10bit`. The CICP is written in both the sequence header and `colr`, HDR10 (HD-5's fixed values) in both SVT-AV1's metadata OBUs and `mdcv`/`clli`; ffprobe's MP4 colour comes from `colr`, so H2's `trace_headers` is what catches a mislabelled bitstream. The owner-clip half of the CRF table was re-calibrated against `hevc_10bit`, which scores above 8-bit `hevc` (96.075 against 95.469 at Format default); the spike half stands at 8 bits. (orig C2)
- **G-17 closed on the WebM path by one reader per output (CX-15 (2)).** C3 met one hang, a video pump blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with the audio pump gone (#379). Cancelling a shared reader from the other thread is what G-17 measured crashing 12 of 30 cancels, so each pump now reads and cancels its own `AVAssetReader`; R1 measured the two-reader read equal frame for frame and sample for sample. #378 then did the same for `ExportWriter`. Every WebM stop is logged (`export.webm`), the Opus FIFO is fed by bytes, and the sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), not by count. (orig C3, C3 fix pass)
- **VP9's depth is the picture's, and the WebM Colour is its only transfer label (CX-16).** `sdr` is Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709; `hlg`/`pq` are Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020. libvpx's bitstream carries a colour space but no transfer, so HLG and PQ live only in the container. (orig S §7, C4)
- **An SDR WebM copy is labelled from its source (CX-16 (10), RULING-1).** V10 re-imported Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` with cyan coming back (23, 255, 255): BT.709 decoded as BT.601, because the rewrap's copy carried no colour and AVFoundation chose the matrix by size. The copy now carries the Colour's codes, else a VP9 keyframe's `color_space` for the matrix (`stream_matrix`); V10 then read 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96 of 255. (orig C4 "RULING-1")
- **VP9 alpha is a second encoder (CX-17).** libvpx has no alpha input; the alpha plane is a second 8-bit picture (Y = round(255·a), full range, chroma 128) at constant quality, keys forced on the same frames, packets paired by pts, written as BlockAdditional 1 with `AlphaMode` 1 and a ReferenceBlock on non-keys. Presets 10 and 12 came within 0.7 VMAF of HEVC: no row. (orig S §2)
- **VP9 is for the web and alpha, not efficiency (CX-3).** libvpx good-4 needs 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality, but 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's; good-2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 % more time, rt-8 only HEVC's quality. (orig S §2)
- **The encoders are static, platform-side, built by `make codecs` (CX-4, CX-5).** No nasm, yasm, meson or ninja is needed on arm64 (Neon C intrinsics); cmake from Homebrew and the system perl are. The cold build is about 30 s; the stamp makes a warm one a no-op. Linked and stripped, SVT-AV1 adds 3.33 MB and libvpx 1.59 MB. `libSvtAv1Enc.a` carries `vector.c` (MIT), whose notice ships only through #376's acknowledgements (PUB-10). (orig S §1, C0)

It is a second `ExportPipeline`, the one exception to §7.8's one writer, sharing the reader outputs, the pump, the gain, #337's end, the chapter partition, the size and the rates. (orig S §3, C3)
- **AV1 in MP4 goes through a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (CX-12).** `canAdd` answered true for `av01`, and every frame decoded md5-identical. The core builds `av1C` from a full parse of the sequence header OBU, strips temporal delimiters and patches the `ftyp` to carry `av01`, which AV1-ISOBMFF requires and `AVAssetWriter` does not write (`rc_av1_*`). The writer reads sync samples from the bitstream itself: both `all-sync` and `no-sync` survived, so the attachment code went and A5's key-flag match is the guard. (orig S §3, C1, C1 fix pass)
- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. Capped CRF replaced it, calibrated so each tier matches or beats HEVC's VMAF at HEVC's rate on the spike's three clips and on the owner's 55 s 1080p clip through the app itself, because SvtAv1EncApp's command-line scores did not transfer (1.1 VMAF lower for SVT-AV1 at one CRF and 1.6 for HEVC on that clip). A strict cap (12 % overshoot) left Faster under HEVC at Format default (a plateau at 95.055–95.348 against 95.469), because SVT-AV1 budgets each window's keyframes and base layers under the cap; SVT's default 50 % overshoot met every comparator. (orig C1 fix pass)
- **`av1` is always 10-bit, an HDR row (CX-14).** AV1's Main profile decodes 8 and 10 bits alike and only higher-quality exports matter, so there is no `av1_10bit`. The CICP is written in both the sequence header and `colr`, HDR10 (HD-5's fixed values) in both SVT-AV1's metadata OBUs and `mdcv`/`clli`; ffprobe's MP4 colour comes from `colr`, so H2's `trace_headers` is what catches a mislabelled bitstream. The owner-clip half of the CRF table was re-calibrated against `hevc_10bit`, which scores above 8-bit `hevc` (96.075 against 95.469 at Format default); the spike half stands at 8 bits. (orig C2)
- **G-17 closed on the WebM path by one reader per output (CX-15 (2)).** C3 met one hang, a video pump blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with the audio pump gone (#379). Cancelling a shared reader from the other thread is what G-17 measured crashing 12 of 30 cancels, so each pump now reads and cancels its own `AVAssetReader`; R1 measured the two-reader read equal frame for frame and sample for sample. #378 then did the same for `ExportWriter`. Every WebM stop is logged (`export.webm`), the Opus FIFO is fed by bytes, and the sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), not by count. (orig C3, C3 fix pass)
- **VP9's depth is the picture's, and the WebM Colour is its only transfer label (CX-16).** `sdr` is Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709; `hlg`/`pq` are Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020. libvpx's bitstream carries a colour space but no transfer, so HLG and PQ live only in the container. (orig S §7, C4)
- **An SDR WebM copy is labelled from its source (CX-16 (10), RULING-1).** V10 re-imported Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` with cyan coming back (23, 255, 255): BT.709 decoded as BT.601, because the rewrap's copy carried no colour and AVFoundation chose the matrix by size. The copy now carries the Colour's codes, else a VP9 keyframe's `color_space` for the matrix (`stream_matrix`); V10 then read 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96 of 255. (orig C4 "RULING-1")
- **VP9 alpha is a second encoder (CX-17).** libvpx has no alpha input; the alpha plane is a second 8-bit picture (Y = round(255·a), full range, chroma 128) at constant quality, keys forced on the same frames, packets paired by pts, written as BlockAdditional 1 with `AlphaMode` 1 and a ReferenceBlock on non-keys. AV1 alpha does not exist in practice (no API input, no Matroska mapping). The frames are straightened first (G-35). The alpha level is banded by size so every band holds 48 dB at its worst frame (C5 fix pass, RULING-1). (orig S §4, C5, C5 fix pass)
- **The memory limit is a ledger, not a pool (CX-18).** The queue stays one job at a time; a bundled-encoder job is held while the app's running encoder exports (the queue's and every Export… sheet's) and it would pass a quarter of physical memory, each costed by its measured peak per key, scaled by pixels. A sheet is counted, never held; a held job is passed over and says why. On a 32 GiB Mac that admits one AV1 job at 4K at any speed; on 16 GiB one AV1 4K job always runs alone. (orig C6a)
- **The estimate is fitted on real footage (CX-18 amended by C6b).** C6a's single-run constants, on AV.mov scaled up, were 50–79 % short of real footage. C6b took idle three-run medians on the GH5 4K clip, fitting a fixed start from a 250-frame and a 50-frame batch; `av1_webm` copies `av1`'s times (within 10 %). (orig C6a, C6b)

**The proofs.** `codecs_proof.py` (L1–L3, the libraries' versions); `av1_export_proof.py` (Z1, A1–A9, H1–H5, S1–S3; `--rate` adds R1 and R2, the cap share and VMAF against `hevc_10bit` on the owner's clip); `webm_export_proof.py` (Z1, W1–W13, S4, the fault rows F1–F3, `--readers` R1, and `webm_audio_probe.swift`'s P1–P5 and A1–A5); `vp9_export_proof.py` (Z1, V1–V11, S1, P1; `--rate` R1–R3) with `vp9_rate_probe.swift`; `vp9_alpha_export_proof.py` (Z1, A1–A12, S1, P1) with `vp9_alpha_probe.swift`; `encoder_limit_proof.py` (P0, R1, R2, Q1–Q5, E1–E3, S1, S2, X1, Z1; `--probe` runs `encoder_limit_probe.swift` with no app); `encoder_memory_measure.py` (the instrument the cost tables are transcribed from, with `--derive`); `export_offset_proof.py` E36–E43 (clicks against flashes on every new row); `export_readers_proof.py` (#378); `hdr_proof.py` H7s; `build_codecs.py --selftest`. Every phase passed `make gate`.

## Known limits

- **AV1 cannot be decoded on an M1 or M2** (CX-10): the export works, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 file there, and the proofs read AV1 through ffmpeg; playback is SE-17 and SE-18 on an M3 or later.
- **A soft cap, not a ceiling** (CX-13, CX-16 (7)): a file usually stays under its rate but can pass it, measured up to 1.254 × on AV1 and 1.143 × on VP9; the guide says about 1.25 × and 1.15 ×. The calibration is four clips at 1080p, one of them binding, and other sizes are placed by bits per pixel alone.
- **Faster at Maximum sits 0.059 VMAF under `hevc_10bit`** (CX-14 (6), the owner's "Best CRF, accept 0.06"): below CRF 12 the cap binds and a lower CRF gains nothing.
- **Thin margins against a moving comparator**: VideoToolbox's `hevc` and `hevc_10bit` read a few hundredths differently run to run (95.338 and 95.469; one 10-bit encode 0.25 lower under load), and VP9's 8-bit Medium (+0.016) and Format default (+0.029) cells are kept by that much.
- **The spike half of AV1's calibration stands at 8 bits** (CX-14 (6)); only the owner-clip half was re-run against `hevc_10bit`.
- **A `vp9_alpha_webm` re-imports opaque** (CX-17 (7)): the rewrap copies the Block and not the BlockAdditional, and Apple's VP9 decoder has no alpha (#381). ffmpeg's native `vp9` decoder ignores the alpha too; only libvpx's reads it. Safari's playback is SE-21's question.
- **No HDR or 10-bit alpha, no AV1 alpha, no VP9 in MP4** (CX-1, CX-17 (8)).
- **One VP9 speed** (CX-3, CX-16 (2)): the Speed popup is disabled on the VP9 rows.
- **The HDR rendering is a person's** (HDR-8): ffmpeg's Matroska demuxer exports no content-light-level side data when MaxFALL is 0, which HD-5's fixed values make it, though the walk reads MaxCLL 1000 / MaxFALL 0 in the Colour.
- **Opus undershoots its rate**: AudioToolbox at 192 kb/s wrote about 119 kb/s on A1's sound (CX-7).
- **The cost tables are one machine and one picture** (CX-18): a heavier timeline or harder footage can exceed a peak or take longer, and a sheet export can take the app past the budget (CX-18 (6)). VP9's estimate runs 12–14 % high at 1440p, its per-frame time growing slower than the pixels between the two measured sizes; within the tolerance and not re-tuned.
- **GIF and APNG are outside the ledger**: a 4K GIF peaked 11.48 GiB and a 4K APNG 7.85 GiB above baseline (C6b's A), neither booked because neither is a writer row (#383).

- #377, the brief: every phase built; closed by the close's commit.
- #376 (acknowledgements, `ef3414f`) and #378 (G-17 on `ExportWriter`, `d0f9fe0`): closed.
- #379: open. C3's one unreproduced hang, the WebM audio pump stopping early; one reader per output closed the starvation it caused, but its cause was not found in 42 later exports.
- #381: open. Keeping a `vp9_alpha_webm`'s alpha on re-import (C5's "to file").
- #382: open. An `av1` MP4 export hung once in `encoder_limit_proof.py`'s Q1, its video read stuck in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with no compositor request in flight (C5's fix pass).
- #383: open. 4K GIF and APNG memory outside the encoder limit (C6b's finding 2).
- #380: open, filed beside #376's acknowledgements: whether the LGPL-2 JavaScriptCore inside the bun-compiled assistant helper needs more than a notice. Not this road map's code.
- Nothing else is known to be unfinished, so no issue was filed at the close.

Not filed, each decided:
- C3's re-review nit: no app row shows `align`'s gap fill or head cut (E40 does not show whether the first buffer straddled the in point); `webm_audio_probe.swift`'s A1–A5 are its proof.
- VP9's 1440p over-estimate: within CX-18's 25 % tolerance, recorded above.
- `AgentCatalog+Render.swift` at 402 lines after C5's merge, past the 400 a new file starts under: its next text pays a toll first (the size rule).
- Every `rc_*` wrapper lands in `ReelCore.swift`, over the ~600 cap, so each new export pays a toll there: the standing rule in `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` ("Any addition to `ReelCore.swift` pays for itself first"), followed by C1, C3 and C5.
- C4's `export_gain_proof.py --against …/gain-before` was not run (no control on that host); H7i's first failure was a missing control capture, not the change (orig C4 fix pass).
- The `CLAUDE.md` edits each phase listed as owed are all in the per-side files and the root file.

## Where to look in the original

- "Goal", "The owner's choices" and "The orchestrator's defaults": the brief's binding rows and the defaults the owner may change.
- "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)": the export table, writer, WebM reader, build and bridge the phases started from.
- "Phases": what each phase was to build, and its acceptance.
- "S — the spike": the instruments and test clips; §1 the pins, build commands, build times, link sizes and licences of libaom, SVT-AV1, libvpx, libopus and libwebm; §2 the VMAF, speed and RSS tables per encoder and preset, and the recommendation; §3 AV1 and VP9 in MP4 (`av1C`, TDs, the `ftyp` brand, no AV1 decode on M2) and libwebm against a core writer; §4 alpha and the browsers; §5 AudioToolbox's Opus; §6 the frame path's conversion costs, queue and memory; §7 HDR per codec and container; "Risks".
- "C0 — decisions and the encoder build": the pins' digests, the build's commands and outputs, D36–D41, `vector.c`.
- "C1 — AV1 in MP4": the tolls, the row, the VBR rate runs, the nine mutants and the equivalent `all-sync`/`open-gop`; its "Fix pass 1": the capped-CRF calibration (spike and through the app), the strict cap's failure, the four options put to the owner and Ruling 2.
- "C2 — AV1 at 10 bits, with HLG, PQ and HDR10": the 10-bit calibration, the outlier `hevc_10bit` encode, the Faster-at-Maximum ruling, H4's code values and the nine mutants.
- "C3 — AV1 in WebM, with Opus": the tolls, the writer's files, the eight mutants, ffmpeg's readings of key flags, CodecDelay and MaxFALL, the hang; its fix pass: one reader per output, F1–F3, the FIFO by bytes, `align`.
- "C4 — VP9 in WebM, 8-bit and Profile 2 HDR": RULING-1 and its import measurements, the CQ calibration and libvmaf's index pairing, the ten mutants; its "Fix pass 1": the rebase onto #378, the nits and H7s's and H7i's controls.
- "C5 — VP9 with alpha in WebM": the tolls, the alpha's calibration, the mutants; its "Fix pass 1": the rebase onto C6a, the alpha row's memory run, RULING-1's size bands and the `av1` hang.
- "C6a — the Export Queue's memory limit and the sheet's estimate": the first memory and time table, what the limit means per RAM size, Q1–Q5 and the ten mutants; its "Fix pass 1": the tooltip, `phase7_chrome.py`'s band and `graphic/tests/path.rs`'s CPU-time budget.
- "C6b — 4K on every row and the final time constants": the idle-machine protocol and loads, the 4K AVFoundation and image rows, the derive's intercepts, the memory winners, the speed claims, the held-out check and the APNG counting fix.

## Context

Before this road map Frame Job exported H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. The owner's brief (2026-10-27) asked for AV1 and VP9 with the encoders bundled, and fixed four rows (AV1 in MP4 with AAC, AV1 in WebM with Opus, VP9 in WebM with Opus, VP9 with alpha in WebM; VP9 in MP4 not wanted), SVT-AV1 at three speeds (Faster 8, Balanced 6, Smaller file 4), libvpx at one, and a Rust WebM writer in the core rather than libwebm. The rest were the orchestrator's defaults, each the owner's to change: AudioToolbox's Opus, AV1 HDR first and VP9 Profile 2 later, pinned tarballs with no vendored source, the bitrate semantics kept, the M1/M2 decode gap documented, the encoders platform-side. Standing owner rules applied throughout: only higher-quality exports matter, memory limits relative to physical RAM, no feature size budget, person-only checks in `docs/manual-checks.md`. (orig "Goal", "The owner's choices", "The orchestrator's defaults", "How it fits the tree (at `75fd806`)")

## Decisions

- **SVT-AV1, not libaom (CX-2, the spike).** At matched quality SVT-AV1 preset 4 equalled libaom good-5/6 (Δ VMAF over HEVC +3.36 against +3.67/+3.57 on `real8`, +5.11 against +4.96/+4.88 on `gh5`) at about 41 fps against 13.6–16, about 3× faster; at matched speed SVT 8 gave +2.56 against libaom rt-8's +1.37. libaom's best (good-3/4) is about 0.8 VMAF above SVT 4 at about 11× the time. libaom's favour: a higher worst frame (92 against 88) and half the memory. Presets 10 and 12 came within 0.7 VMAF of HEVC: no row. (orig S §2)
- **VP9 is for the web and alpha, not efficiency (CX-3).** libvpx good-4 needs 16–26 % less bitrate than HEVC for its quality, but 1.4–1.7× SVT 6's; good-2 bought +0.14–0.43 VMAF for about 35 % more time, rt-8 only HEVC's quality. (orig S §2)
- **The encoders are static, platform-side, built by `make codecs` (CX-4, CX-5).** No nasm, yasm, meson or ninja is needed on arm64 (Neon C intrinsics); cmake from Homebrew and the system perl are. The cold build is about 30 s; the stamp makes a warm one a no-op. Linked and stripped, SVT-AV1 adds 3.33 MB and libvpx 1.59 MB. `libSvtAv1Enc.a` carries `vector.c` (MIT), whose notice ships only through #376's acknowledgements (PUB-10). (orig S §1, C0)
- **The WebM writer is the core's (CX-6, CX-15).** Container bytes are decisions (timestamps, clusters, cues, CodecDelay), not sample work, as #216-R drew the line; the spike's libwebm files read back through the core's reader, which is the round-trip the core's tests now make against the writer. It is a second `ExportPipeline`, the one exception to §7.8's one writer, sharing the reader outputs, the pump, the gain, #337's end, the chapter partition, the size and the rates. (orig S §3, C3)
- **AV1 in MP4 goes through a passthrough `AVAssetWriterInput` (CX-12).** `canAdd` answered true for `av01`, and every frame decoded md5-identical. The core builds `av1C` from a full parse of the sequence header OBU, strips temporal delimiters and patches the `ftyp` to carry `av01`, which AV1-ISOBMFF requires and `AVAssetWriter` does not write (`rc_av1_*`). The writer reads sync samples from the bitstream itself: both `all-sync` and `no-sync` survived, so the attachment code went and A5's key-flag match is the guard. (orig S §3, C1, C1 fix pass)
- **AV1's rate is a soft cap, quality first (CX-13; the owner chose option 2, 2026-10-28).** Single-pass VBR (CX-9) undershot a real clip to 0.667–0.670 of its target. Capped CRF replaced it, calibrated so each tier matches or beats HEVC's VMAF at HEVC's rate on the spike's three clips and on the owner's 55 s 1080p clip through the app itself, because SvtAv1EncApp's command-line scores did not transfer (1.1 VMAF lower for SVT-AV1 at one CRF and 1.6 for HEVC on that clip). A strict cap (12 % overshoot) left Faster under HEVC at Format default (a plateau at 95.055–95.348 against 95.469), because SVT-AV1 budgets each window's keyframes and base layers under the cap; SVT's default 50 % overshoot met every comparator. (orig C1 fix pass)
- **`av1` is always 10-bit, an HDR row (CX-14).** AV1's Main profile decodes 8 and 10 bits alike and only higher-quality exports matter, so there is no `av1_10bit`. The CICP is written in both the sequence header and `colr`, HDR10 (HD-5's fixed values) in both SVT-AV1's metadata OBUs and `mdcv`/`clli`; ffprobe's MP4 colour comes from `colr`, so H2's `trace_headers` is what catches a mislabelled bitstream. The owner-clip half of the CRF table was re-calibrated against `hevc_10bit`, which scores above 8-bit `hevc` (96.075 against 95.469 at Format default); the spike half stands at 8 bits. (orig C2)
- **G-17 closed on the WebM path by one reader per output (CX-15 (2)).** C3 met one hang, a video pump blocked in `copyNextSampleBuffer` with the audio pump gone (#379). Cancelling a shared reader from the other thread is what G-17 measured crashing 12 of 30 cancels, so each pump now reads and cancels its own `AVAssetReader`; R1 measured the two-reader read equal frame for frame and sample for sample. #378 then did the same for `ExportWriter`. Every WebM stop is logged (`export.webm`), the Opus FIFO is fed by bytes, and the sound is placed at its stamps (`ExportAudioEnd.align`), not by count. (orig C3, C3 fix pass)
- **VP9's depth is the picture's, and the WebM Colour is its only transfer label (CX-16).** `sdr` is Profile 0 8-bit I420 BT.709; `hlg`/`pq` are Profile 2 10-bit I010 BT.2020. libvpx's bitstream carries a colour space but no transfer, so HLG and PQ live only in the container. (orig S §7, C4)
- **An SDR WebM copy is labelled from its source (CX-16 (10), RULING-1).** V10 re-imported Frame Job's own 640 × 360 SDR `vp9_webm` with cyan coming back (23, 255, 255): BT.709 decoded as BT.601, because the rewrap's copy carried no colour and AVFoundation chose the matrix by size. The copy now carries the Colour's codes, else a VP9 keyframe's `color_space` for the matrix (`stream_matrix`); V10 then read 1.90 / 0.55 / 0.96 of 255. (orig C4 "RULING-1")
- **VP9 alpha is a second encoder (CX-17).** libvpx has no alpha input; the alpha plane is a second 8-bit picture (Y = round(255·a), full range, chroma 128) at constant quality, keys forced on the same frames, packets paired by pts, written as BlockAdditional 1 with `AlphaMode` 1 and a ReferenceBlock on non-keys. AV1 alpha does not exist in practice (no API input, no Matroska mapping). The frames are straightened first (G-35). The alpha level is banded by size so every band holds 48 dB at its worst frame (C5 fix pass, RULING-1). (orig S §4, C5, C5 fix pass)
- **The memory limit is a ledger, not a pool (CX-18).** The queue stays one job at a time; a bundled-encoder job is held while the app's running encoder exports (the queue's and every Export… sheet's) and it would pass a quarter of physical memory, each costed by its measured peak per key, scaled by pixels. A sheet is counted, never held; a held job is passed over and says why. On a 32 GiB Mac that admits one AV1 job at 4K at any speed; on 16 GiB one AV1 4K job always runs alone. (orig C6a)
- **The estimate is fitted on real footage (CX-18 amended by C6b).** C6a's single-run constants, on AV.mov scaled up, were 50–79 % short of real footage. C6b took idle three-run medians on the GH5 4K clip, fitting a fixed start from a 250-frame and a 50-frame batch; `av1_webm` copies `av1`'s times (within 10 %). (orig C6a, C6b)

## Known limits

- **AV1 cannot be decoded on an M1 or M2** (CX-10): the export works, but Frame Job cannot preview or re-import its own AV1 file there, and the proofs read AV1 through ffmpeg; playback is SE-17 and SE-18 on an M3 or later.
- **A soft cap, not a ceiling** (CX-13, CX-16 (7)): a file usually stays under its rate but can pass it, measured up to 1.254 × on AV1 and 1.143 × on VP9; the guide says about 1.25 × and 1.15 ×. The calibration is four clips at 1080p, one of them binding, and other sizes are placed by bits per pixel alone.
- **Faster at Maximum sits 0.059 VMAF under `hevc_10bit`** (CX-14 (6), the owner's "Best CRF, accept 0.06"): below CRF 12 the cap binds and a lower CRF gains nothing.
- **Thin margins against a moving comparator**: VideoToolbox's `hevc` and `hevc_10bit` read a few hundredths differently run to run (95.338 and 95.469; one 10-bit encode 0.25 lower under load), and VP9's 8-bit Medium (+0.016) and Format default (+0.029) cells are kept by that much.
- **The spike half of AV1's calibration stands at 8 bits** (CX-14 (6)); only the owner-clip half was re-run against `hevc_10bit`.
- **A `vp9_alpha_webm` re-imports opaque** (CX-17 (7)): the rewrap copies the Block and not the BlockAdditional, and Apple's VP9 decoder has no alpha (#381). ffmpeg's native `vp9` decoder ignores the alpha too; only libvpx's reads it. Safari's playback is SE-21's question.
- **No HDR or 10-bit alpha, no AV1 alpha, no VP9 in MP4** (CX-1, CX-17 (8)).
- **One VP9 speed** (CX-3, CX-16 (2)): the Speed popup is disabled on the VP9 rows.
- **The HDR rendering is a person's** (HDR-8): ffmpeg's Matroska demuxer exports no content-light-level side data when MaxFALL is 0, which HD-5's fixed values make it, though the walk reads MaxCLL 1000 / MaxFALL 0 in the Colour.
- **Opus undershoots its rate**: AudioToolbox at 192 kb/s wrote about 119 kb/s on A1's sound (CX-7).
- **The cost tables are one machine and one picture** (CX-18): a heavier timeline or harder footage can exceed a peak or take longer, and a sheet export can take the app past the budget (CX-18 (6)). VP9's estimate runs 12–14 % high at 1440p, its per-frame time growing slower than the pixels between the two measured sizes; within the tolerance and not re-tuned.
- **GIF and APNG are outside the ledger**: a 4K GIF peaked 11.48 GiB and a 4K APNG 7.85 GiB above baseline (C6b's A), neither booked because neither is a writer row (#383).

the Metal compositor, media import and its caches, and agent dispatch. No
pixel or sample work in Rust; no ffmpeg dependency in the product. The AV1 and
VP9 encoders (SVT-AV1, libvpx; road map `designs/codec-export.md`) are
platform-side like AVFoundation: Swift calls them through the bridging header,
no `rc_*` export wraps them (spec §11 CX-4).

  4. **risk accepted:** a rate is a target, and single-pass SVT-AV1 undershot it by 14–22 % on
     5 s clips (libvpx overshot by 5–7 %). C1 re-measures on a full-length export. *Result
     (C1):* on the owner's 55 s 1080p30 clip single-pass VBR at Balanced came in at
     0.667–0.670 of the target in six runs, at "Format default" and at High
     (`designs/codec-export.md`, C1); the owner then chose capped constant quality for the
     AV1 rows, CX-13, which replaces (1) and this item there.


**Runs (2026-10-27).** Debug and Release 13/13; `--rate` on Release 15/15 (the
undershoot printed: 0.667–0.670 of the target in all six runs). Seven mutants
were caught exactly; `all-sync` and `open-gop` survived, recorded in
`designs/codec-export.md`'s C1 findings. `encode-ignores-cancel` was caught
only after A6 waited for the loudness measurement to end before cancelling.
**Fix pass 1** (the same day, capped CRF, CX-13): `all-sync` and its inverse
`no-sync` (every sample `NotSync`) both survived — the passthrough writer reads
the sync samples from the bitstream — so the pump's attachment and both mutants
went; `open-gop` is caught (exit 1, A5 and Z1) now that the rate is CRF, since
SVT-AV1 forces KF refresh only under single-pass VBR. Under a strict 12 % cap
`--rate` failed R1 and R2 (the owner's clip under `hevc`'s VMAF); the owner chose a
soft cap (SVT's 50 %, each file at most 1.25 × the cap, raised to 1.30 × at C1's integration), and on the final tree
`--rate` on Release scored 15/15 (`designs/codec-export.md`'s C1 fix pass 1).

**Runs (C2, 2026-10-28).** Debug 19/19 (on the table before C2's calibration, and again
after the owner's Faster-at-Maximum ruling, CRF 12);
`hdr_proof.py --only DR,Z1` 2/2 on Debug and on Release; the nine C2-touched mutants
each `MUTANT CAUGHT` with exactly their rows. Release `--rate` first scored 20/21: R1
failed against a `hevc_10bit` at 96.075 where the 10-bit calibration's single encode
had read 95.828; seven re-encodes read 96.075 each, Format default's three CRFs were
lowered against it, and the second Release `--rate` scored 21/21
(`designs/codec-export.md`'s C2).
